The Erdős minimum overlap problem seeks to find a step function that minimizes the maximum overlap with its complement under arbitrary shifts. The current solution uses local optimization techniques that can get trapped in suboptimal regions. The proposed approach leverages Bayesian optimization with an explicit surrogate model to guide the search more efficiently through the highly non-convex space of step functions. Bayesian optimization balances exploration and exploitation by maintaining a probabilistic model of the objective function, allowing it to intelligently prioritize regions likely to yield improvements.

This transformation dramatically reduces the effective dimensionality of the optimization problem while preserving essential structural information. The algorithm begins with coarse resolutions to rapidly identify promising regions of the search space, then increases resolution in these regions before performing local refinement.

This method addresses the main bottlenecks of existing approaches: (1) Slow convergence due to dimensionality, (2) Inability to escape local optima, and (3) Insufficient exploration of abstract functional forms.
